findingDetails.case: The inspected checkout has .skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env containing SYSTEM_HOOKS_DISABLED=1, while the battery process environment does not define that variable; the suppression row is PASS and does not report the active disable.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The suppression row may intentionally display only environment values, but that leaves an effective persisted disable invisible and conflicts with the battery's stated coverage of suppression flags.
claimAdjudication.claim: The setup battery can report no suppression while the target checkout's persistent hook flag store disables Git hooks.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the shared hook reader is environment-only and whether the battery reads the persisted file through another path; the reader explicitly loads hook-flags.env, and the checker does not.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the supported hook contract removes persistent hook-flags.env settings for Git preflight or the checker is explicitly scoped and labeled as environment-only.

findingDetails.description: checkSuppression reads only process.env. The shared hook-flags store also reads the target checkout's .skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env, and git-preflight-advisory uses that store to disable itself. With SYSTEM_HOOKS_DISABLED=1 saved in that file and absent from the process environment, the battery reports suppression PASS with no detail although the actual hook is disabled.
findingDetails.recommendation: Read the inspected checkout's hook-flags.env with the shared parser and precedence rules, without loading code from that checkout, and report/fail on effective master or preflight disables.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The checker filters process.env at lines 561-565; hook-flags.cjs resolves its default config file at lines 83-89 and consults it when no injected config is supplied at lines 151-173. The preflight hook exits early when isHookEnabled returns false at lines 76-81.
findingDetails.title: Persistent hook disable flags are invisible to the suppression check

findingDetails.case: With --tool codex, .codex/hooks.json contains hooks.SessionStart with command 'echo git-preflight-advisory' and no PreToolUse entry; the checker sees the substring and reports registered although Git commands never trigger the advisory.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: A marker-only probe may have been chosen to avoid depending on every runtime schema, but it cannot establish that the runtime invokes this advisory on Git commands.
claimAdjudication.claim: The active AI-tool hook check can mark a non-triggering Codex configuration as registered.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Compared the positive Codex fixture with the repository's documented adapter contract and checked whether the matcher requires an exact event or command; it only searches serialized hook content for the marker.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the supported Codex contract makes the tested SessionStart marker invoke the preflight for each Git command, or if the check is relabeled as marker presence rather than registration.

findingDetails.description: registersAdvisory accepts any occurrence of git-preflight-advisory anywhere under a runtime file's hooks section. The Codex test fixture places only a marker command under SessionStart and asserts PASS, while the documented Codex integration registers the executable on PreToolUse with matcher exec. An inert or wrong-event entry therefore satisfies the active-tool check.
findingDetails.recommendation: Validate each runtime's actual event, matcher, and executable target; make positive fixtures match the documented runtime schema and add inert/wrong-event negative fixtures.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The implementation serializes the whole selected section and performs substring matching at lines 580-583. The Codex positive test uses SessionStart at lines 337-344, while the integration contract specifies PreToolUse and matcher exec in hooks/README.md:78.
findingDetails.title: AI hook registration passes on a marker string in the wrong event

findingDetails.case: If a later change makes JSON status treat SKIP or UNKNOWN as failure while the exit code remains based only on FAIL, a JSON run whose rows are PASS/SKIP or PASS/UNKNOWN returns status FAIL with exit 0; the existing JSON assertion still uses a fixture with an actual FAIL and would not distinguish this regression.
findingDetails.description: The JSON test checks report.status and process status only on a fixture that already contains a FAIL. The human-mode test covers a no-FAIL run with a SKIP, but no JSON test covers a no-FAIL SKIP or UNKNOWN result. The implementation currently shares the failed-row predicate, so this is a regression guard gap rather than an observed runtime mismatch.
findingDetails.recommendation: Add a JSON fixture with no FAIL and at least one SKIP, plus an UNKNOWN-only/no-FAIL case, and assert report.status and process status both remain OK/0.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The sole JSON behavior test asserts aggregation at lines 130-155 using a normal fixture; the no-fail SKIP case at lines 174-176 is human mode only.
findingDetails.title: JSON outcome tests do not cover UNKNOWN/SKIP-only runs
